title: The Story of the Greeks
author: H. A. Guerber
licenseEvidence: Project Gutenberg #23495: "Public domain in the USA"; title page reads "Copyright, 1896, by American Book Company" (published 1896)
description: H. A. Guerber's classic 1896 read-aloud tells the story of ancient Greece in short, lively chapters, from the old myths and the Trojan War through Marathon, Pericles, Socrates, and Alexander to the Roman conquest. It suits the whole family in grades 3–6: each day you read one chapter aloud, your child narrates it back, finds the place on a map, and adds it to a timeline. The full text is free online.
includes: 115 lessons in 15 units, one chapter per lesson
Link to the free full text for every chapter
Narration prompt, map work, and timeline entry for each lesson
Parent notes flagging myth told as history, dated viewpoints, and mature content

lessons.title: Chapter 1: Early Inhabitants of Greece
steps: Read Chapter I, "Early Inhabitants of Greece," aloud together
Narration: tell who lived in Greece long ago and who came by sea to teach them
Map work: Find Greece, the Mediterranean Sea, Egypt, and Phoenicia on a map; notice the islands like stepping-stones
Timeline: Add "Pelasgians live in Greece" at c. 2000 BC (the book's estimate)
questions: How did the earliest Greeks, the Pelasgians, live?
Why did Egyptian and Phoenician sailors hop from island to island instead of crossing open sea?
answers: In forests and caves, hunting with clubs and stone-tipped weapons and wearing animal skins
They had no compass, so they stayed in sight of land
lessons.notes: The book dates events by Bible stories ("when Isaac went to Egypt"). Modern historians describe early Greece differently; treat the Egyptian-teacher story as an old tradition.

lessons.title: Chapter 2: The Deluge of Ogyges
steps: Read Chapter II, "The Deluge of Ogyges," aloud together
Narration: tell how Inachus helped the Pelasgians and what happened in the great flood
Map work: Find Argos on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Deluge of Ogyges" to the myths strip of your timeline (legend, no real date)
questions: Why did later Greeks call the huge old stone walls "Cyclopean"?
Which city did Inachus found?
answers: They said one-eyed giants called Cyclopes must have built them
Argos
lessons.notes: Inachus and Ogyges are legendary figures, though the giant "Cyclopean" walls are real and can still be seen.

lessons.title: Chapter 3: The Founding of Many Important Cities
steps: Read Chapter III, "The Founding of Many Important Cities," aloud together
Narration: name the founders in this chapter and what each one gave the Greeks
Map work: Find Athens, Thebes, Argos, Mycenae, and the Isthmus of Corinth on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Mycenae's great walls and gold masks" at c. 1600–1200 BC; put Cecrops and Cadmus on the myths strip
questions: What very important gift did Cadmus bring to Greece?
Whose name was given to the city of Athens?
What surprising things were found in the old tombs at Mycenae?
answers: The alphabet (writing)
The goddess Athene
Thin masks of pure gold, plus weapons, armor, and pottery
lessons.notes: Cecrops, Cadmus, and Danaus are founders from legend. The Mycenae finds are real (dug up in 1876).

lessons.title: Chapter 4: Story of Deucalion
steps: Read Chapter IV, "Story of Deucalion," aloud together
Narration: tell the story of Deucalion and Pyrrha after the flood
Map work: Find Thessaly, Delphi, and the pass of Thermopylae on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Deucalion's flood" to the myths strip; add "Amphictyonic Council meets at Delphi" (a real league, its beginning is legendary)
questions: What did Deucalion decide "your mother's bones" meant?
What does the name Thermopylae mean?
answers: The stones of the Earth
The Hot Gateway (hot springs in a narrow pass)
lessons.notes: The Deucalion story is a myth; the book says so.

lessons.title: Chapter 5: Story of Dædalus and Icarus
steps: Read Chapter V, "Story of Dædalus and Icarus," aloud together
Narration: tell how Daedalus and Icarus escaped from Crete
Map work: Find Crete and the Icarian Sea on a map
Timeline: Add "Daedalus and Icarus" and "King Minos of Crete" to the myths strip
questions: Which useful inventions does the book credit to Daedalus?
Why did Icarus fall into the sea?
Who were the Hellenes named after?
answers: The saw, the potter's wheel, and sails for ships
He flew too near the sun and the wax holding his wings melted
Hellen, son of Deucalion
lessons.notes: The book suggests the wing story grew out of Daedalus inventing sails. That is the author's guess; the Minoan civilization on Crete was real.

lessons.title: Chapter 6: The Adventures of Jason
steps: Read Chapter VI, "The Adventures of Jason," aloud together
Narration: tell who the heroes were and what Jason went looking for
Map work: Find the Peloponnesus, then trace the Argo's route from Greece across the Black Sea to Colchis
Timeline: Add "Voyage of the Argo" to the myths strip
questions: How many heroes sailed on the Argo?
What did the Golden Fleece really stand for, according to the book?
Where does the name Peloponnesus come from?
answers: Fifty
The riches the Greeks brought home from trading in the East
Pelops, who ruled the peninsula
lessons.notes: Jason's voyage is legend; the book explains it as an early trading journey.

lessons.title: Chapter 7: Theseus Visits the Labyrinth
steps: Read Chapter VII, "Theseus Visits the Labyrinth," aloud together
Narration: tell how Theseus beat the monster in the Labyrinth, and what happened to his father
Map work: Find Athens, Crete, the Aegean Sea, and the island of Scyros
Timeline: Add "Theseus and the Labyrinth" to the myths strip
questions: How did Theseus find his way out of the Labyrinth?
Why did King Aegeus think his son was dead?
What festival did Theseus start for Athene?
answers: By following a long thread the king's daughter gave him
The ship came back with black sails instead of white
The Panathenaea
lessons.notes: Theseus is a legendary hero. The Acropolis named here is real and still stands in Athens.

lessons.title: Chapter 8: The Terrible Prophecy
steps: Read Chapter VIII, "The Terrible Prophecy," aloud together
Narration: tell why baby Oedipus was sent away and how he ended up in Corinth
Map work: Find Thebes, Delphi, and Corinth on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Oedipus" to the myths strip
questions: Why did King Laius want to get rid of his baby son?
What does the name Oedipus mean?
answers: An oracle said the son would kill his father and bring ruin to the city
Swollen-footed
lessons.notes: The Oedipus myth spans three chapters and has dark themes (a man unknowingly marries his mother). Preview it and shorten or skip parts if needed for younger children.

lessons.title: Chapter 9: The Sphinx's Riddle
steps: Read Chapter IX, "The Sphinx's Riddle," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened at the crossroads and how Oedipus beat the Sphinx
Map work: Find Thebes in Boeotia and trace a road toward Delphi
Timeline: Add "The Sphinx's riddle" to the myths strip next to Oedipus
questions: What was the Sphinx's riddle, and what was the answer?
What did the Sphinx look like?
answers: What walks on four feet in the morning, two at noon, and three at night? Man
A woman's head, a lion's body, and an eagle's wings
lessons.notes: Myth. The violence at the crossroads is told plainly; you may want to summarize it.

lessons.title: Chapter 10: Blindness and Death of Œdipus
steps: Read Chapter X, "Blindness and Death of Œdipus," aloud together
Narration: tell how the truth about Oedipus came out and what Antigone did
Map work: Find Thebes again and talk about how far a blind man could wander on foot
questions: What did the oracle say would stop the plague in Thebes?
Which daughter stayed to guide her blind father?
answers: Finding and punishing the man who killed King Laius
Antigone
lessons.notes: Contains Jocasta's suicide and Oedipus blinding himself. Read ahead and soften or summarize for younger listeners.

lessons.title: Chapter 11: The Brothers' Quarrel
steps: Read Chapter XI, "The Brothers' Quarrel," aloud together
Narration: tell why Eteocles and Polynices fought and how their quarrel ended
Map work: Find Argos, Nemea, and Thebes and trace the march of the Seven
Timeline: Add "Seven against Thebes" to the myths strip; note the real Nemean Games
questions: What was the brothers' agreement, and who broke it?
Which games did the seven chiefs start, and in whose honor?
How long did the first siege of Thebes last?
answers: To rule a year each in turn; Eteocles broke it
The Nemean Games, honoring Hercules' victory over the Nemean lion
Seven years
lessons.notes: The book itself says this family story is a myth.

lessons.title: Chapter 12: The Taking of Thebes
steps: Read Chapter XII, "The Taking of Thebes," aloud together
Narration: tell how the sons of the Seven finally took Thebes
Map work: Find Thebes and Argos on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "War of the Epigoni" to the myths strip
questions: What does "Epigoni" mean?
Who was put on the throne of Thebes after it was taken?
answers: Descendants (the sons of the first warriors)
Thersander, son of Polynices

units.title: Unit 2: Troy, Homer, and the End of the Heroic Age (Chapters 13–20)

lessons.title: Chapter 13: The Childhood of Paris
steps: Read Chapter XIII, "The Childhood of Paris," aloud together
Narration: tell the story of Paris from his mother's dream to his journey home with Helen
Map work: Find Troy in Asia Minor (modern Turkey), Sparta, and the port of Aulis
Timeline: Add "Paris and Helen" to the myths strip, beginning the Trojan War story
questions: What did Queen Hecuba dream about baby Paris?
How was Paris recognized when he came to Troy?
Where did Menelaus tell his allies to gather?
answers: A flaming brand in his cradle that set the palace on fire
He won all the prizes at the games, looked like the royal family, and Cassandra named him
Aulis
lessons.notes: The Trojan War comes from Homer's poems. Troy was a real city, but the story with gods and heroes is legend, not proven history.

lessons.title: Chapter 14: The Muster of the Troops
steps: Read Chapter XIV, "The Muster of the Troops," aloud together
Narration: tell who the Greek chiefs were and how Ulysses found Achilles
Map work: Find Aulis and the island of Scyros
Timeline: Add "Greek army gathers at Aulis" to the myths strip
questions: Why was Achilles' heel the only place he could be hurt?
How did Ulysses trick Achilles into showing who he was?
Who was chosen leader of the whole Greek army?
answers: His mother held him by the heel when she dipped him in the river Styx
He put a fine sword among his trinkets, and only Achilles grabbed it
Agamemnon, King of Mycenae

lessons.title: Chapter 15: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
steps: Read Chapter XV, "The Sacrifice of Iphigenia," aloud together
Narration: tell why the Greek fleet could not sail and what happened once they reached Troy
Map work: Trace the route from Aulis across the Aegean Sea to Troy
Timeline: Add "Siege of Troy begins" to the myths strip (ancient Greeks placed it near 1200 BC)
questions: Why was there no wind to carry the Greek ships?
How long had the war gone on before anyone was close to winning?
answers: Agamemnon had offended the goddess Diana, and the oracle said she must be appeased
Nine years
lessons.notes: The story of a father asked to sacrifice his daughter is upsetting; the book has the goddess rescue her. A good chance to talk about myths versus history.

lessons.title: Chapter 16: The Wrath of Achilles
steps: Read Chapter XVI, "The Wrath of Achilles," aloud together
Narration: tell why Achilles stopped fighting and what made him return
Map work: Find the plain between Troy and the sea where the armies camped
Timeline: Add "The Wrath of Achilles (the Iliad)" to the myths strip
questions: Why did Achilles refuse to fight for Agamemnon?
Whose armor did Patroclus wear into battle, and who killed him?
answers: Agamemnon unfairly took away the captive girl given to Achilles
Achilles' armor; Hector killed him
lessons.notes: The book mentions captives being made slaves. Gods sending a plague is part of the myth.

lessons.title: Chapter 17: Death of Hector and Achilles
steps: Read Chapter XVII, "Death of Hector and Achilles," aloud together
Narration: tell about the fight between Hector and Achilles and King Priam's visit
Map work: Find Troy and imagine the walls the old king watched from
Timeline: Add "Death of Hector and Achilles" to the myths strip
questions: Why did old King Priam secretly visit Achilles' tent?
How did Achilles die?
answers: To beg for the body of his son Hector so he could bury it
A poisoned arrow shot by Paris hit his heel

lessons.title: Chapter 18: The Burning of Troy
steps: Read Chapter XVIII, "The Burning of Troy," aloud together
Narration: tell how the wooden horse tricked the Trojans
Map work: Find Troy, then Sicily and southern Italy ("Great Greece"), and the Tiber River where Aeneas landed
Timeline: Add "Fall of Troy" to the myths strip (Greek tradition said c. 1184 BC); add the real "Troy excavated by Schliemann, 1870s" to the modern end
questions: Whose idea was the wooden horse?
Why did the Trojans tear down part of their own wall?
Which Trojan prince escaped to start a new kingdom in Italy?
answers: Ulysses
The horse was too big to fit through the gates
Aeneas
lessons.notes: Archaeologists did find a burned city at Troy, but the wooden horse and the heroes are legend.

lessons.title: Chapter 19: Heroic Death of Codrus
steps: Read Chapter XIX, "Heroic Death of Codrus," aloud together
Narration: tell how King Codrus saved Athens
Map work: Find the Peloponnesus (the "mulberry leaf"), Sparta, Athens, and the Ionian cities of Ephesus and Miletus in Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Dorians move into the Peloponnesus" at c. 1100 BC and "Death of Codrus" at c. 1070 BC (traditional date)
questions: What had the oracle promised about the coming battle?
Why did Codrus dress as an ordinary soldier?
What title did the Athenians give their rulers after Codrus instead of king?
answers: The army whose king was killed would win
So the enemy would not recognize him and spare him
Archon
lessons.notes: The book says real history begins here. Codrus is still partly legendary; written records came later.

lessons.title: Chapter 20: The Blind Poet
steps: Read Chapter XX, "The Blind Poet," aloud together
Narration: tell what we know about Homer and how his poems spread
Map work: Find the island of Chios and the coast of Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Homer's Iliad and Odyssey" at c. 750 BC
questions: What are Homer's two great poems about?
How were Homer's poems kept alive before they were written down?
Which island was most often named as Homer's birthplace?
answers: The Iliad tells of the Trojan War; the Odyssey of Ulysses' ten-year voyage home
People memorized and recited them from place to place
Chios
lessons.notes: The pirate-blinding story is a legend; historians are not sure Homer was one real person.

units.title: Unit 3: Sparta and the Laws of Lycurgus (Chapters 21–28)

lessons.title: Chapter 21: The Rise of Sparta
steps: Read Chapter XXI, "The Rise of Sparta," aloud together
Narration: tell how Lycurgus protected the baby king
Map work: Find Sparta and Laconia on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Lycurgus gives Sparta its laws" at c. 800 BC (traditional date)
questions: Who were the Helots?
Why did Sparta have two kings at once?
How did Lycurgus keep the baby king Charilaus safe?
answers: Prisoners of war who became Spartan slaves
Aristodemus's twin sons both became king, and each line continued
He pretended to agree to kill him, then took him to the council hall and had him named king
lessons.notes: Many historians think Lycurgus may be partly or wholly legendary.

lessons.title: Chapter 22: The Spartan Training
steps: Read Chapter XXII, "The Spartan Training," aloud together
Narration: describe a Spartan boy's life after age seven
Map work: Find the Eurotas River near Sparta
Timeline: Add "Spartan training system" alongside Lycurgus (c. 800–600 BC)
questions: At what age were Spartan children given over to the state?
What did Spartan boys sleep on?
answers: Seven
A pile of rushes from the Eurotas River
lessons.notes: The chapter describes leaving weak babies to die. Read ahead and decide how to handle it.

lessons.title: Chapter 23: The Brave Spartan Boy
steps: Read Chapter XXIII, "The Brave Spartan Boy," aloud together
Narration: tell the story of the boy and the fox, and what "laconic" means
Map work: Find Laconia, the land around Sparta
questions: Why were Spartan boys trained to steal food?
What does "laconic" speech mean, and where does the word come from?
answers: Spartan armies had no supply wagons and had to find their own food in war
Saying a lot in few words; from Laconia, the land of Sparta
lessons.notes: The book praises harsh customs (flogging, the fox story). Ask your child whether these customs were good or wise.

lessons.title: Chapter 24: Public Tables in Sparta
steps: Read Chapter XXIV, "Public Tables in Sparta," aloud together
Narration: describe the Spartan common tables and what mothers told sons going to war
Map work: Find Sparta and Messenia next to it
questions: What was the Spartan men's favorite food?
What did a Spartan mother say when handing her son his shield, and what did she mean?
answers: Black broth, a thick dark stew
"Come back with it or on it": come home with honor or die bravely
lessons.notes: The book describes deliberately getting a slave drunk as a lesson, a cruel custom worth discussing.

lessons.title: Chapter 25: Laws of Lycurgus
steps: Read Chapter XXV, "Laws of Lycurgus," aloud together
Narration: tell what Lycurgus did about money and how he made the laws last
Map work: Find Sparta and talk about how hard it would be to cart heavy iron money there
Timeline: Add "Sparta uses iron money" next to Lycurgus
questions: Why did Lycurgus make the Spartans use iron money?
How did Lycurgus make sure the laws would be kept after he left?
answers: It was so heavy that no one could hide it, steal it, or grow greedy for wealth
He made the citizens swear to obey them until he came back, then never returned
lessons.notes: Story of the oath is a legend about a figure who may not have existed.

lessons.title: Chapter 26: The Messenian War
steps: Read Chapter XXVI, "The Messenian War," aloud together
Narration: tell why Sparta attacked Messenia and what happened at Ithome
Map work: Find Messenia and Mount Ithome west of Sparta
Timeline: Add "First Messenian War" at c. 743–724 BC
questions: Why did the Spartans want Messenia's land?
Why couldn't the Spartans climb up to Ithome?
answers: Its fields were more fertile than their own
It stood on a very high, steep rock and the defenders rolled stones down
lessons.notes: Includes a king sacrificing his daughter and then taking his own life. Preview before reading aloud.

lessons.title: Chapter 27: The Music of Tyrtæus
steps: Read Chapter XXVII, "The Music of Tyrtæus," aloud together
Narration: tell how a lame schoolmaster helped the Spartans win
Map work: Find Messenia, Sparta, and Athens
Timeline: Add "Second Messenian War" at c. 685–668 BC
questions: What bold thing did Aristomenes do inside Sparta?
Whom did the Athenians send to lead the Spartans, and how did he help?
answers: He hung a trophy of captured arms in the main temple and wrote his name under it
Tyrtaeus, a lame schoolmaster, who stirred them with war songs

lessons.title: Chapter 28: Aristomenes' Escape
steps: Read Chapter XXVIII, "Aristomenes' Escape," aloud together
Narration: tell how Aristomenes got out of the pit
Map work: Find Messenia, then Sicily, the city of Messina, and the Strait of Messina
Timeline: Add "Messenians found colonies in Italy and Sicily" at c. 650 BC
questions: What animal led Aristomenes out of the pit?
Which city in Sicily was named after the Messenians' homeland?
answers: A fox
Messina
lessons.notes: The escape story is a legend told about a real war.

units.title: Unit 4: The Olympic Games and the Lawgivers of Athens (Chapters 29–35)

lessons.title: Chapter 29: The Olympic Games
steps: Read Chapter XXIX, "The Olympic Games," aloud together
Narration: describe the Olympic games: where, how often, and what the winners received
Map work: Find Elis and Olympia, northwest of Sparta
Timeline: Add "First recorded Olympic games" at 776 BC (the book says 774) and "Modern Olympics revived in Athens" at AD 1896
questions: What prize did Olympic winners receive?
How did Greeks use the games to count time?
Where were the first modern Olympics held, and when?
answers: A crown of wild olive leaves
They counted by Olympiads, the four-year spans between games
Athens, in 1896
lessons.notes: Hercules founding the games is legend. The book was written in 1896, the year the modern games began, so it calls them brand new.

lessons.title: Chapter 30: Milo of Croton
steps: Read Chapter XXX, "Milo of Croton," aloud together
Narration: tell how Milo became so strong and how he died
Map work: Find Croton in southern Italy (a Greek colony)
Timeline: Add "Milo of Croton, Olympic wrestler" at c. 540–510 BC
questions: How did Milo train to grow stronger each day?
What trapped Milo in the forest?
answers: He carried a calf every day as it grew into an ox
His hands got caught when a split tree trunk snapped shut
lessons.notes: Milo was a real champion wrestler, but stories like eating a whole ox are exaggerated legends.

lessons.title: Chapter 31: The Jealous Athlete
steps: Read Chapter XXXI, "The Jealous Athlete," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened to the jealous man and to the statue
Map work: Find Olympia again on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Theagenes, champion athlete" at c. 480 BC
questions: How did the jealous man die?
What punishment did the judges give the statue?
answers: He shook the statue until it fell and crushed him
It was thrown into the sea
lessons.notes: Good chance to discuss what the book calls superstition.

lessons.title: Chapter 32: The Girls' Games
steps: Read Chapter XXXII, "The Girls' Games," aloud together
Narration: describe the girls' torch race and the chariot races
Map work: Find Olympia and sketch a stadium and a hippodrome
questions: How did a girl win the torch race?
Where were the horse and chariot races held?
answers: By reaching the goal first with her torch still lit, or keeping it lit longest
In the hippodrome
lessons.notes: Girls' races at Olympia were held at a separate festival honoring the goddess Hera.

lessons.title: Chapter 33: The Bloody Laws of Draco
steps: Read Chapter XXXIII, "The Bloody Laws of Draco," aloud together
Narration: tell about Draco's laws and what happened to Cylon's followers
Map work: Find Athens, the Acropolis, and the island of Aegina
Timeline: Add "Cylon tries to seize Athens" at c. 632 BC and "Draco's laws" at c. 621 BC (the book says 602)
questions: Why do we still call very harsh rules "draconian"?
What punishment did Draco set for stealing a cabbage?
Why did Cylon's men hold a cord tied to Athene's statue?
answers: Draco's laws punished small wrongs as severely as great crimes
Death
They believed it kept them under the goddess's protection

lessons.title: Chapter 34: The Laws of Solon
steps: Read Chapter XXXIV, "The Laws of Solon," aloud together
Narration: tell what Solon changed in Athens
Map work: Find Athens and the Areopagus hill beside the Acropolis
Timeline: Add "Solon's laws" at 594 BC
questions: Why were trials at the Areopagus held in the dark?
How long did Epimenides sleep in the cave?
How long did Solon ask the Athenians to keep his laws while he traveled?
answers: So the jury would judge by the facts, not by how the accused looked
Fifty-eight years
Ten years
lessons.notes: Epimenides' long sleep is a legend (like Rip Van Winkle).

lessons.title: Chapter 35: The First Plays
steps: Read Chapter XXXV, "The First Plays," aloud together
Narration: tell how Greek plays began and what the Theater of Dionysus was like
Map work: Find Athens and the Theater of Dionysus below the Acropolis
Timeline: Add "Thespis, first actor" at c. 534 BC
questions: What does "tragedy" mean in Greek?
Why did Solon dislike the plays?
Name one Greek writer of tragedies and one of comedies.
answers: Goat song
He said they taught people to love a lie
Tragedies: Aeschylus, Sophocles, or Euripides; comedies: Aristophanes
lessons.notes: Actors are still called "thespians" after Thespis.

units.title: Unit 5: Tyrants of Athens and the Great King (Chapters 36–41)

lessons.title: Chapter 36: The Tyrant Pisistratus
steps: Read Chapter XXXVI, "The Tyrant Pisistratus," aloud together
Narration: tell how Pisistratus tricked his way to power and what good he did
Map work: Find Athens and its Acropolis
Timeline: Add "Pisistratus becomes tyrant" at 561 BC
questions: What trick did Pisistratus use to get a bodyguard?
Which two English words come from the Greek "aristoi" and "demos"?
What did Pisistratus do with Homer's poems?
answers: He wounded himself and said nobles had attacked him
Aristocrat and democrat
Had them written down and put in a public library

lessons.title: Chapter 37: The Tyrant's Insult
steps: Read Chapter XXXVII, "The Tyrant's Insult," aloud together
Narration: tell why Harmodius and Aristogiton turned against the tyrants
Map work: Find Athens; Solon had been traveling in Asia Minor across the Aegean
Timeline: Add "Death of Pisistratus; his sons rule" at 527 BC
questions: How did Solon feel when he came home and found Pisistratus ruling?
How did Hipparchus insult Harmodius?
answers: Sorry at first, but he forgave him because he ruled wisely
He banned Harmodius's sister from carrying flowers in the procession

lessons.title: Chapter 38: Death of the Conspirators
steps: Read Chapter XXXVIII, "Death of the Conspirators," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened at the festival and how Leaena kept the secret
Map work: Find Athens on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Hipparchus killed" at 514 BC
questions: Which tyrant did Harmodius kill?
What image was put on Leaena's tomb, and why?
answers: Hipparchus
A lioness without a tongue, because she kept silent under torture
lessons.notes: Contains torture; you may want to summarize Leaena's story.

lessons.title: Chapter 39: Hippias Driven Out of Athens
steps: Read Chapter XXXIX, "Hippias Driven Out of Athens," aloud together
Narration: tell how Hippias was driven out and how ostracism worked
Map work: Find Delphi, Athens, and Sparta
Timeline: Add "Hippias driven out" at 510 BC and "Clisthenes' reforms" at 508 BC
questions: How did the Alcmaeonidae win the favor of the priests at Delphi?
What was written on the shells in an ostracism vote?
How many votes were needed to ostracize a man?
answers: They rebuilt the temple in white marble, paying the extra cost themselves
The name of the man to be banished
Six thousand

lessons.title: Chapter 40: The Great King
steps: Read Chapter XL, "The Great King," aloud together
Narration: describe the Great King and how he ruled his huge empire
Map work: Find Persia, Ecbatana, and Ionia on the coast of Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Darius I becomes king of Persia" at 522 BC
questions: What were satraps?
What was special about the walls of Ecbatana?
answers: Governors who ruled the provinces (satrapies) for the king
There were seven walls, each painted a different bright color

lessons.title: Chapter 41: Hippias Visits Darius
steps: Read Chapter XLI, "Hippias Visits Darius," aloud together
Narration: tell how a Greek doctor helped make Darius want to conquer Greece
Map work: Trace a route from Persia across Asia Minor to Greece
Timeline: Add "Democedes, Greek doctor at the Persian court" at c. 520 BC
questions: How did Democedes become the king's doctor?
Why did Darius decide to conquer Greece?
answers: He healed the king's hurt foot after the Persian doctors failed
His officers' reports on Greece made him curious, and Hippias urged him on
lessons.notes: The book tells this mostly from the historian Herodotus; scholars think the real reasons for the war were more political.

lessons.title: Chapter 42: Destruction of the Persian Host
steps: Read Chapter XLII, "Destruction of the Persian Host," aloud together
Narration: tell why Darius was angry with the Athenians and what happened to his first army and fleet
Map work: Find Sardis, Ionia, the Hellespont, and Mount Athos
Timeline: Add "Ionian Revolt; Sardis burned" at 499–498 BC and "Persian fleet wrecked off Mount Athos" at 492 BC
questions: What did Darius's slave say to him every day at dinner?
What destroyed the Persian fleet near Mount Athos?
answers: "Master, remember the Athenians!"
A terrible storm

lessons.title: Chapter 43: The Advance of the Second Host
steps: Read Chapter XLIII, "The Advance of the Second Host," aloud together
Narration: tell how Athens and Sparta answered Darius and how Miltiades came to command
Map work: Find Marathon, Athens, Sparta, and Plataea
Timeline: Add "Persians demand earth and water" at 491 BC
questions: What did "earth and water" stand for?
Why did the Spartans say they could not come at once?
How did Miltiades become sole commander?
answers: Accepting the Persian king as master of their land and sea
They believed they had to wait until the moon was full
Aristides and the other generals gave him their days of command

lessons.title: Chapter 44: The Battle of Marathon
steps: Read Chapter XLIV, "The Battle of Marathon," aloud together
Narration: tell the story of the Battle of Marathon and the runner who carried the news
Map work: Find Marathon on a map of Greece and measure about how far it is to Athens
Timeline: Add "Battle of Marathon" at 490 BC
questions: Who attacked first at Marathon?
What did the runner say when he reached Athens?
Why did Miltiades march his tired army straight back to Athens?
answers: The Greeks
"Rejoice, we have conquered!"
To defend the city in case the Persian fleet sailed there
lessons.notes: The famous Marathon runner story is a later legend, the origin of today's marathon race. Some of the gory details can be skipped.

lessons.title: Chapter 45: Miltiades' Disgrace
steps: Read Chapter XLV, "Miltiades' Disgrace," aloud together
Narration: tell how Athens honored Miltiades and how he fell from favor
Map work: Find the Acropolis in Athens and the island of Paros
Timeline: Add "Miltiades dies in disgrace" at 489 BC
questions: What was made from the captured Persian shields and arms?
Why was Miltiades put on trial?
Who was Miltiades' son?
answers: A huge statue of Athene on the Acropolis
He used the fleet to attack Paros over a personal quarrel and failed
Cimon

lessons.title: Chapter 46: Aristides the Just
steps: Read Chapter XLVI, "Aristides the Just," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened when the farmer asked Aristides to write on his shell
Map work: Find Athens and the market place (agora)
Timeline: Add "Aristides ostracized" at 482 BC
questions: What did Themistocles and Aristides disagree about?
Why did the farmer want Aristides banished?
What did Aristides write on the shell?
answers: Themistocles wanted more ships; Aristides wanted a bigger land army
He was tired of hearing him called "the Just"
His own name

lessons.title: Chapter 47: Two Noble Spartan Youths
steps: Read Chapter XLVII, "Two Noble Spartan Youths," aloud together
Narration: tell what Bulis and Sperthias offered Xerxes and how he answered
Map work: Find Sparta and Persia
Timeline: Add "Darius dies; Xerxes becomes king" at 486 BC
questions: Why did Bulis and Sperthias go to Persia?
Why wouldn't they bow before Xerxes?
answers: To offer their lives to make up for the Persian messengers Sparta had killed
They said such honor belonged only to their gods
lessons.notes: The army sizes here (two million) come from ancient writers; modern historians think it was far smaller.

lessons.title: Chapter 48: The Great Army
steps: Read Chapter XLVIII, "The Great Army," aloud together
Narration: describe Xerxes' army crossing the Hellespont
Map work: Find the Hellespont and the canal at Mount Athos
Timeline: Add "Xerxes crosses the Hellespont" at 480 BC
questions: What did Xerxes do after a storm wrecked his bridges?
Why did Xerxes weep when he looked at his army?
Who were the Immortals?
answers: Had the waves whipped and chains thrown into the strait
In a hundred years every one of those men would be dead
The king's bodyguard of picked soldiers

lessons.title: Chapter 49: Preparations for Defense
steps: Read Chapter XLIX, "Preparations for Defense," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Greeks prepared to meet Xerxes
Map work: Find Corinth, Thermopylae, and Artemisium
Timeline: Add "Greek council at Corinth" at 481 BC
questions: Why did so few soldiers go with Leonidas?
How many Spartans went to guard Thermopylae?
answers: Most Greeks were at the Olympic games and believed it was wrong to fight during them
Three hundred

lessons.title: Chapter 50: Leonidas at Thermopylæ
steps: Read Chapter L, "Leonidas at Thermopylæ," aloud together
Narration: tell how Leonidas and his men held the pass
Map work: Find Thermopylae on a map of Greece and look at the narrow strip between mountains and sea
Timeline: Add "Battle of Thermopylae" at 480 BC
questions: What did Leonidas answer when told to give up his weapons?
What did he say about the arrows darkening the sun?
answers: "Come and take them!"
"Then we can fight in the shade."
lessons.notes: The "fight in the shade" line is usually credited to the Spartan Dieneces in Herodotus.

lessons.title: Chapter 51: Death of Leonidas
steps: Read Chapter LI, "Death of Leonidas," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Persians got around the Greeks at Thermopylae and what happened next
Map work: Find Thermopylae, Delphi, Artemisium, and the Isthmus of Corinth
Timeline: Add "Death of Leonidas" at 480 BC (same year as Thermopylae)
questions: Who showed the Persians the secret path?
Which allies stayed to die with the Spartans?
What did the Greeks start building across the Isthmus of Corinth?
answers: Ephialtes, a Greek shepherd
Seven hundred Thespians
A huge wall
lessons.notes: The storm at Delphi is told as if the gods protected their temple; this comes from Herodotus.

lessons.title: Chapter 52: The Burning of Athens
steps: Read Chapter LII, "The Burning of Athens," aloud together
Narration: tell what "wooden walls" meant and what happened to Athens
Map work: Find Athens and the Bay of Salamis
Timeline: Add "Persians burn Athens" at 480 BC
questions: What did Themistocles say the "wooden walls" were?
Where did the Athenian families go?
What did Themistocles say when Eurybiades raised his staff?
answers: Their ships
To the Peloponnesus
"Strike if you will, but hear me!"

lessons.title: Chapter 53: The Battles of Salamis and Platæa
steps: Read Chapter LIII, "The Battles of Salamis and Platæa," aloud together
Narration: tell about the victories at Salamis and Plataea, and Pausanias's two suppers
Map work: Find Salamis, Plataea, and Mycale (on the coast of Asia Minor)
Timeline: Add "Battle of Salamis" at 480 BC and "Battles of Plataea and Mycale" at 479 BC
questions: Who rowed out to warn the Greek fleet of Xerxes' plan?
Where did Xerxes watch the sea battle from?
What point did Pausanias make with the two suppers?
answers: Aristides
A throne on a mountain
That the plain Spartans had beaten the luxurious Persians
lessons.notes: The Greek commander at Mycale was actually the Spartan king Leotychides, not Eurybiades as the book says.

units.title: Unit 7: The Golden Age of Athens (Chapters 54–59)

lessons.title: Chapter 54: The Rebuilding of Athens
steps: Read Chapter LIV, "The Rebuilding of Athens," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Athenians rebuilt their city and how Themistocles fooled the Spartans
Map work: Find Athens, Sparta, and Miletus
Timeline: Add "Walls of Athens rebuilt" at 478 BC
questions: What "good omen" encouraged the Athenians?
How did Themistocles give Athens time to finish the walls?
answers: A new shoot grew from the burned sacred olive tree
He drew out the talks in Sparta until the walls were high enough

lessons.title: Chapter 55: Death of Pausanias
steps: Read Chapter LV, "Death of Pausanias," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened to Pausanias and to Themistocles
Map work: Find Sparta, then Persia, where Themistocles ended his life
Timeline: Add "Pausanias dies" at c. 470 BC and "Themistocles ostracized" at c. 471 BC
questions: What wrong did Pausanias do?
What did Themistocles refuse to do for the Persian king?
answers: He secretly offered to help the Persians if they made him king of all Greece
Lead a Persian army against the Greeks
lessons.notes: Mentions starvation and suicide; summarize if needed.

lessons.title: Chapter 56: Cimon Improves Athens
steps: Read Chapter LVI, "Cimon Improves Athens," aloud together
Narration: tell how Aristides and Cimon each served Athens
Map work: Find Athens, the island of Scyros, and the Theseum (Temple of Hephaestus) in Athens
Timeline: Add "Theseus's bones brought to Athens" at c. 475 BC and "Death of Aristides" at c. 468 BC
questions: How rich was Aristides when he died?
What did the Athenians wrongly do with the allies' money?
Where did Athenians go to hear philosophers?
answers: So poor there was not enough to pay for his funeral
Spent it to beautify their own city instead of on the army and navy
The gardens of the Academy (and the Lyceum)
lessons.notes: The bones were believed to be Theseus's; the building called the Theseum is actually a temple of Hephaestus.

lessons.title: Chapter 57: The Earthquake
steps: Read Chapter LVII, "The Earthquake," aloud together
Narration: tell how Cimon changed and what happened after the earthquake at Sparta
Map work: Find Sparta and Messenia, and Athens to the northeast
Timeline: Add "Great earthquake at Sparta; Helots revolt" at 464 BC and "Cimon ostracized" at 461 BC
questions: Who scolded the young Cimon for being lazy?
How did Cimon help poor people who were too proud to ask?
Why did the Athenians ostracize Cimon?
answers: Aristides the Just
His servants found out their needs and helped them secretly
They were angry that the Spartans had insulted the army Cimon urged them to send

lessons.title: Chapter 58: The Age of Pericles
steps: Read Chapter LVIII, "The Age of Pericles," aloud together
Narration: tell what Pericles built and how Cimon served Athens one last time
Map work: Find the Acropolis, the Parthenon, and the port of Piraeus with the Long Walls
Timeline: Add "Parthenon built" at 447–432 BC and "Thirty Years' Peace" at 446 BC
questions: What did the Long Walls connect?
Who made the carvings and great statue for the Parthenon?
Why was Cimon's death kept secret for a month?
answers: Athens and its seaport, Piraeus
Phidias
So the army could get used to a new leader without losing courage

lessons.title: Chapter 59: The Teachings of Anaxagoras
steps: Read Chapter LIX, "The Teachings of Anaxagoras," aloud together
Narration: tell what Anaxagoras taught about the sun and moon and why he was exiled
Map work: Find Athens and the Peloponnesus (Anaxagoras guessed the sun was about as big as the Peloponnesus)
Timeline: Add "Anaxagoras teaches in Athens" at c. 460–430 BC
questions: What did Anaxagoras say the sun really was?
What did he think the moon was like?
answers: A great glowing rock, not a god in a chariot
Much like the earth, with mountains, plains, and seas
lessons.notes: The author writes from a 19th-century Christian viewpoint (Anaxagoras "had never heard of the true God"). Adjust the framing to suit your family.

lessons.title: Chapter 60: Beginning of the Peloponnesian War
steps: Read Chapter LX, "Beginning of the Peloponnesian War," aloud together
Narration: tell how Pericles explained the eclipse to his pilot
Map work: Find Attica, Athens, Piraeus, and the Peloponnesus
Timeline: Add "Peloponnesian War begins" at 431 BC
questions: What was Pericles' plan for fighting Sparta?
How did Pericles show his pilot what an eclipse is?
answers: Bring everyone inside the city walls and fight with the navy at sea
He threw his cloak over the man's head, blocking the sun the way the moon does
lessons.notes: Try the cloak demonstration with a lamp and a ball.

lessons.title: Chapter 61: Death of Pericles
steps: Read Chapter LXI, "Death of Pericles," aloud together
Narration: tell about the plague in Athens and Pericles' last words
Map work: Find Athens and the island of Cos, home of Hippocrates
Timeline: Add "Plague in Athens" at 430 BC and "Death of Pericles" at 429 BC
questions: Why did Hippocrates refuse the Persian king's offer?
What was Pericles proudest of as he died?
answers: He said his duty was to save his own countrymen first
That he never caused any fellow citizen to put on mourning
lessons.notes: Hippocrates was a real doctor, but the story of his coming to cure Athens is a later legend. Some plague descriptions are grim.

lessons.title: Chapter 62: The Philosopher Socrates
steps: Read Chapter LXII, "The Philosopher Socrates," aloud together
Narration: tell what kind of man and teacher Socrates was
Map work: Find Athens on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Socrates teaching in Athens" at c. 430–399 BC
questions: What was Socrates' trade?
What did Socrates say after being drenched with water?
answers: A stonecutter
"After the thunder comes the rain."
lessons.notes: The book's view of Xanthippe as a scold comes from old anecdotes and is unkind; little is really known about her. The author also reads Christian ideas into Socrates.

lessons.title: Chapter 63: Socrates' Favorite Pupil
steps: Read Chapter LXIII, "Socrates' Favorite Pupil," aloud together
Narration: tell what Alcibiades was like as a boy and how Socrates saved him
Map work: Find the Academy outside Athens where Socrates taught
Timeline: Add "Socrates saves Alcibiades in battle" at c. 432 BC
questions: Name Socrates' three famous pupils from this chapter.
What did little Alcibiades do when a wagon would not stop?
Why was Alcibiades in danger in his first battle?
answers: Plato, Xenophon, and Alcibiades
He lay down in the road and dared the driver to come on
His showy gold armor was weak and his flatterers left him

lessons.title: Chapter 64: Youth of Alcibiades
steps: Read Chapter LXIV, "Youth of Alcibiades," aloud together
Narration: tell about the tricks Alcibiades played to get people talking
Map work: Find Olympia, where Alcibiades raced his chariots
Timeline: Add "Alcibiades wins at Olympia" at 416 BC
questions: Why did Alcibiades cut off his dog's tail?
How was Alcibiades different from Nicias?
answers: To give the Athenians something to talk about
Alcibiades was bold and ambitious; Nicias was careful and slow

lessons.title: Chapter 65: Greek Colonies in Italy
steps: Read Chapter LXV, "Greek Colonies in Italy," aloud together
Narration: tell about the Sybarites and why Athens sent a fleet to Sicily
Map work: Find Sybaris, Croton, and Tarentum in southern Italy, and Syracuse and Messina in Sicily
Timeline: Add "Athenian expedition to Sicily sails" at 415 BC
questions: What does it mean to call someone a Sybarite?
What happened to the statues of Hermes just before the fleet sailed?
answers: A person who loves luxury and ease too much
They were broken, and Alcibiades was blamed

lessons.title: Chapter 66: Alcibiades in Disgrace
steps: Read Chapter LXVI, "Alcibiades in Disgrace," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alcibiades turned against Athens and then tried to help it again
Map work: Find Syracuse, Sparta, and Decelea near Athens
Timeline: Add "Athenian defeat at Syracuse" at 413 BC
questions: Where did Alcibiades go instead of returning to Athens for trial?
What did the Spartans fortify only twelve miles from Athens?
answers: Sparta
Decelea

lessons.title: Chapter 67: Death of Alcibiades
steps: Read Chapter LXVII, "Death of Alcibiades," aloud together
Narration: tell how the war ended and how Alcibiades died
Map work: Find the Chersonese (Gallipoli peninsula) by the Hellespont, then Athens
Timeline: Add "Athenian fleet destroyed at Aegospotami" at 405 BC, "Athens surrenders" at 404 BC, and "Death of Alcibiades" at 404 BC
questions: What did the Spartans tear down to the sound of music?
Who were the Thirty Tyrants?
answers: The Long Walls of Athens
Thirty cruel men the Spartans put in charge of Athens

lessons.title: Chapter 68: The Overthrow of the Thirty Tyrants
steps: Read Chapter LXVIII, "The Overthrow of the Thirty Tyrants," aloud together
Narration: tell how Thrasybulus freed Athens
Map work: Find Athens and Sparta
Timeline: Add "Thrasybulus overthrows the Thirty Tyrants" at 403 BC
questions: Who drove out the Thirty Tyrants?
Why did Sparta have to pay for Lysander's funeral?
answers: Thrasybulus
He kept none of the booty and died poor

lessons.title: Chapter 69: Accusation of Socrates
steps: Read Chapter LXIX, "Accusation of Socrates," aloud together
Narration: tell how a comedy helped turn people against Socrates
Map work: Find Delphi, whose oracle called Socrates the wisest man
Timeline: Add "Aristophanes' play The Clouds" at 423 BC
questions: What did the oracle at Delphi say about Socrates?
Why did Socrates go to see the play that mocked him?
What two charges were made against Socrates?
answers: That he was the most learned (wisest) man in Greece
To find out if any of the faults it showed were ones he could correct
Giving bad advice to young men and speaking ill of the gods

lessons.title: Chapter 70: Death of Socrates
steps: Read Chapter LXX, "Death of Socrates," aloud together
Narration: tell why Socrates would not escape from prison
Map work: Find Athens and the island of Delos
Timeline: Add "Death of Socrates" at 399 BC
questions: Why was Socrates' death delayed a month?
Why did Socrates refuse to escape?
Which pupil wrote down his last conversation?
answers: No one could be executed while the sacred ship was away at Delos
It would be breaking the law, which he had never done
Plato
lessons.notes: This chapter describes his death by poison calmly but in detail. The book again presents Socrates in Christian terms.

lessons.title: Chapter 71: The Defeat of Cyrus
steps: Read Chapter LXXI, "The Defeat of Cyrus," aloud together
Narration: tell why Cyrus fought his brother and what trouble the Greek soldiers were left in
Map work: Find Persia and the Euphrates River near Babylon, where Cunaxa was
Timeline: Add "Battle of Cunaxa" at 401 BC
questions: Why did Cyrus think he should be king instead of Artaxerxes?
What happened to the Greek officers after the battle?
Who came up with a plan to save the Greek army?
answers: He was the first son born after their father became king
They were invited to a council and killed
Xenophon

lessons.title: Chapter 72: The Retreat of the Ten Thousand
steps: Read Chapter LXXII, "The Retreat of the Ten Thousand," aloud together
Narration: describe the long march of the Ten Thousand
Map work: Trace the route from Babylon north through the mountains to the Black Sea and on to Pergamus
Timeline: Add "Retreat of the Ten Thousand" at 401–400 BC
questions: What did Xenophon ask of the soldiers before agreeing to lead?
About how far did the Greeks march to reach the sea?
What is the name of Xenophon's book about the march?
answers: That each would promise to obey him and not quarrel
About a thousand miles
The Anabasis

lessons.title: Chapter 73: Agesilaus in Asia
steps: Read Chapter LXXIII, "Agesilaus in Asia," aloud together
Narration: tell what kind of man and general Agesilaus was
Map work: Find Sparta, then Ionia on the coast of Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Agesilaus fights the Persians in Asia Minor" at 396–394 BC
questions: How did Agesilaus look different from most Spartans?
Why did the Persians think Agesilaus was strange for a king?
answers: He was small, weak, and lame
He dressed like his soldiers and led them himself, without pomp

lessons.title: Chapter 74: A Strange Interview
steps: Read Chapter LXXIV, "A Strange Interview," aloud together
Narration: tell about the meeting under the tree
Map work: Find Asia Minor (Phrygia) where Pharnabazus governed
questions: What was Agesilaus eating when Pharnabazus arrived?
What did the Persian king try when his soldiers could not beat Agesilaus?
answers: Bread and onions
Bribery: he paid Athens and its allies to rise against Sparta

lessons.title: Chapter 75: The Peace of Antalcidas
steps: Read Chapter LXXV, "The Peace of Antalcidas," aloud together
Narration: tell why Agesilaus had to come home and what the Peace of Antalcidas gave away
Map work: Find Coronea in Boeotia and the island of Cyprus
Timeline: Add "Battle of Coronea" at 394 BC and "Peace of Antalcidas (King's Peace)" at 387 BC
questions: What did Agesilaus mean by "ten thousand Persian archers"?
What did the treaty hand over to the Persian king?
answers: Ten thousand Persian coins stamped with an archer, used as a bribe
The Greek cities of Asia Minor and the island of Cyprus

lessons.title: Chapter 76: The Theban Friends
steps: Read Chapter LXXVI, "The Theban Friends," aloud together
Narration: tell how Sparta took Thebes and how Pelopidas and Epaminondas became friends
Map work: Find Thebes in Boeotia
Timeline: Add "Sparta seizes Thebes" at 382 BC
questions: How did the Spartans take Thebes without a fight?
How did Pelopidas and Epaminondas become friends?
answers: They came during a festival when the Thebans were unarmed in the temple
Epaminondas saved the wounded Pelopidas in battle

lessons.title: Chapter 77: Thebes Free Once More
steps: Read Chapter LXXVII, "Thebes Free Once More," aloud together
Narration: tell how twelve exiles freed Thebes
Map work: Trace the road from Athens to Thebes
Timeline: Add "Thebes freed from Sparta" at 379 BC
questions: How did the exiles get into the Spartan banquet?
What did Charon leave with Pelopidas to prove he was loyal?
answers: Dressed as dancing girls
His only son, a baby

lessons.title: Chapter 78: The Battle of Leuctra
steps: Read Chapter LXXVIII, "The Battle of Leuctra," aloud together
Narration: tell about the Sacred Battalion and the Battle of Leuctra
Map work: Find Leuctra in Boeotia, then Laconia
Timeline: Add "Battle of Leuctra: Thebes defeats Sparta" at 371 BC
questions: What oath did the Sacred Battalion take?
What did Epaminondas say about the bad omens?
What terms did Epaminondas give Sparta?
answers: Never to turn their backs on the enemy or surrender
That no omen forbids fighting to defend your country
Never attack Thebes again and set the Messenians free

lessons.title: Chapter 79: Death of Pelopidas
steps: Read Chapter LXXIX, "Death of Pelopidas," aloud together
Narration: tell how Pelopidas was captured, freed, and finally killed
Map work: Find Thessaly in northern Greece
Timeline: Add "Death of Pelopidas" at 364 BC
questions: Why was Pelopidas sent to Thessaly?
How did Epaminondas end up commanding when he was only a soldier?
answers: To warn the cruel tyrant Alexander of Thessaly
The soldiers begged him to lead after their generals failed
lessons.notes: The ending describes harsh treatment of the tyrant's body; skip if needed.

lessons.title: Chapter 80: The Battle of Mantinea
steps: Read Chapter LXXX, "The Battle of Mantinea," aloud together
Narration: tell about Epaminondas's last battle and his last words
Map work: Find Mantinea in the central Peloponnesus
Timeline: Add "Battle of Mantinea; death of Epaminondas" at 362 BC
questions: What two things did the wounded Epaminondas ask about first?
What did he call Leuctra and Mantinea?
answers: How the battle was going and whether his shield was safe
His "daughters," who would keep his name alive

lessons.title: Chapter 81: The Tyrant of Syracuse
steps: Read Chapter LXXXI, "The Tyrant of Syracuse," aloud together
Narration: tell how Philoxenus answered the tyrant's poems
Map work: Find Syracuse on the island of Sicily
Timeline: Add "Dionysius the Elder rules Syracuse" at 405–367 BC
questions: Why did Dionysius send Philoxenus to the Quarries?
What did Philoxenus say the second time he was asked about the poems?
answers: He honestly said the tyrant's poems were trash
"Take me back to the Quarries!"

lessons.title: Chapter 82: Story of Damon and Pythias
steps: Read Chapter LXXXII, "Story of Damon and Pythias," aloud together
Narration: tell the story of Damon and Pythias
Map work: Find Syracuse on a map of Sicily
Timeline: Add "Damon and Pythias" near Dionysius (c. 4th century BC; a famous story)
questions: What did Damon offer to do for Pythias?
Name two things that delayed Pythias on his way back.
What did Dionysius do when Pythias returned?
answers: Stay in prison and die in his place if he did not return
Robbers tied him to a tree; a flooded stream; a hot, dry plain
Set both of them free
lessons.notes: A famous friendship tale, probably more legend than history.

lessons.title: Chapter 83: The Sword of Damocles
steps: Read Chapter LXXXIII, "The Sword of Damocles," aloud together
Narration: tell what Damocles learned at the banquet
Map work: Find Syracuse in Sicily
questions: What was hanging over Damocles' head?
What lesson did Dionysius teach him?
answers: A sword hanging by a single hair
A person always living in fear cannot be truly happy

lessons.title: Chapter 84: Dion and Dionysius
steps: Read Chapter LXXXIV, "Dion and Dionysius," aloud together
Narration: tell how Plato came to Syracuse and what happened to him and Dion
Map work: Find Athens, Syracuse, and Olympia
Timeline: Add "Plato visits Syracuse" at c. 367 BC
questions: Who was Dion's teacher in Athens?
How did the crowd at Olympia honor Plato?
answers: Plato
They gave him an olive crown like a champion's
lessons.notes: Ancient sources place Plato being sold into slavery on his earlier visit to Dionysius the Elder; the book merges the stories.

lessons.title: Chapter 85: Civil War in Syracuse
steps: Read Chapter LXXXV, "Civil War in Syracuse," aloud together
Narration: tell how Dion returned and trapped Dionysius in the citadel
Map work: Find Syracuse and its harbor
Timeline: Add "Dion returns to Syracuse" at 357 BC
questions: Why did Dion come back to Syracuse with an army?
Why did the people start to tire of Dion?
answers: To punish Dionysius, who had forced Dion's wife to marry another man
He was so strict and harsh in demanding virtue and obedience

lessons.title: Chapter 86: Death of Dion
steps: Read Chapter LXXXVI, "Death of Dion," aloud together
Narration: tell how Dionysius's letter turned the people against Dion, and how the tyrant ended up
Map work: Find Syracuse and Corinth
Timeline: Add "Dion murdered" at 354 BC and "Dionysius the Younger exiled to Corinth" at 344 BC
questions: How did Dionysius trick the people into turning against Dion?
What job did Dionysius have at the end of his life in Corinth?
answers: He wrote a letter that made it sound as if Dion wanted to be tyrant
Schoolteacher

units.title: Unit 12: Philip of Macedon and Young Alexander (Chapters 87–94)

lessons.title: Chapter 87: Philip of Macedon
steps: Read Chapter LXXXVII, "Philip of Macedon," aloud together
Narration: tell how Philip became king and how he built his army
Map work: Find Macedon north of Greece, and Thebes where Philip grew up
Timeline: Add "Philip II becomes king of Macedon" at 359 BC
questions: Where did young Philip live as a hostage, and who looked after him?
What was the Macedonian phalanx?
What did the widow mean by appealing "from Philip drunk to Philip sober"?
answers: In Thebes, in the house of Epaminondas
Soldiers packed in a solid block, shields locked, with long spears pointing out in rows
She wanted the king to judge her case again when his head was clear

lessons.title: Chapter 88: Philip Begins His Conquests
steps: Read Chapter LXXXVIII, "Philip Begins His Conquests," aloud together
Narration: tell about Aster's arrow and Demosthenes' speeches
Map work: Find Olynthus and Thrace in the north
Timeline: Add "Demosthenes' first Philippic" at 351 BC
questions: How did Philip treat Nicanor, who spoke badly of him?
What was written on Aster's arrow?
What is a "Philippic"?
answers: Kindly, with a seat at his table and rich gifts
"To Philip's left eye"
A fierce speech against someone, named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip

lessons.title: Chapter 89: The Orator Demosthenes
steps: Read Chapter LXXXIX, "The Orator Demosthenes," aloud together
Narration: tell how Demosthenes taught himself to be a great speaker
Map work: Find Olynthus, which Philip destroyed, and Athens
Timeline: Add "Philip destroys Olynthus" at 348 BC
questions: Why did Demosthenes practice with pebbles in his mouth by the sea?
Why did he shave half his head?
answers: To speak clearly and loudly enough to be heard over the waves
So he would be too embarrassed to go out and would stay home to study
lessons.notes: Good chance to talk about practice and perseverance.

lessons.title: Chapter 90: Philip Masters Greece
steps: Read Chapter XC, "Philip Masters Greece," aloud together
Narration: tell how Philip became master of Greece
Map work: Find Phocis, Delphi, and Chaeronea in Boeotia
Timeline: Add "Battle of Chaeronea" at 338 BC and "Philip is murdered" at 336 BC
questions: Why was the Sacred War fought?
How old was Alexander at Chaeronea, and what did he do there?
What did Demosthenes do during the battle?
answers: The Phocians took land set aside for Apollo and robbed the temple at Delphi
Eighteen; he crushed the Theban Sacred Battalion
He ran away and begged for mercy when a bush caught his cloak

lessons.title: Chapter 91: Birth of Alexander
steps: Read Chapter XCI, "Birth of Alexander," aloud together
Narration: tell about the day Alexander was born and how he was raised
Map work: Find Pella in Macedon and Ephesus in Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Alexander born; Temple of Diana at Ephesus burned" at 356 BC
questions: What three events were said to happen on the day Alexander was born?
Which books did Alexander keep under his pillow?
answers: Parmenio won a victory, Philip's horses won at Olympia, and the Temple of Diana at Ephesus burned
The Iliad and the Odyssey
lessons.notes: The three events falling on one day is an ancient tradition, not certain fact.

lessons.title: Chapter 92: The Steed Bucephalus
steps: Read Chapter XCII, "The Steed Bucephalus," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alexander tamed Bucephalus
Map work: Find Pella and Macedon; Aristotle taught Alexander nearby at Mieza
Timeline: Add "Aristotle becomes Alexander's tutor" at 343 BC
questions: What does "Bucephalus" mean?
What was frightening the horse?
What did Alexander send Aristotle from his travels?
answers: Ox-head
His own shadow
Collections of animals and plants

lessons.title: Chapter 93: Alexander as King
steps: Read Chapter XCIII, "Alexander as King," aloud together
Narration: tell what Alexander did when the Greeks rebelled after Philip died
Map work: Find Thrace, Thebes, and Corinth
Timeline: Add "Alexander becomes king" at 336 BC and "Thebes destroyed" at 335 BC
questions: Why were Demosthenes and the Athenians happy when Philip died?
Which single house did Alexander spare in Thebes?
answers: They thought a young boy could not hold onto power and they would be free
The house of the poet Pindar

lessons.title: Chapter 94: Alexander and Diogenes
steps: Read Chapter XCIV, "Alexander and Diogenes," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened when Alexander visited Diogenes
Map work: Find Corinth on a map of Greece
Timeline: Add "Alexander meets Diogenes" at c. 336 BC
questions: Why did Diogenes throw away his wooden bowl?
What was Diogenes looking for with his lantern?
What did Diogenes ask Alexander to do for him?
answers: He saw a child drink from its hand and decided he didn't need it
An honest man
Stand out of his sunshine
lessons.notes: The story that they died on the same night is an old tradition.

lessons.title: Chapter 95: Alexander's Brilliant Beginning
steps: Read Chapter XCV, "Alexander's Brilliant Beginning," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alexander began his war on Persia
Map work: Find the Hellespont, Troy, the Granicus River, Sardis, Ephesus, and Caria
Timeline: Add "Battle of the Granicus" at 334 BC
questions: What did Alexander say he kept for himself after giving gifts away?
Who saved Alexander's life at the Granicus?
What was Aristotle's "recipe" for a good appetite?
answers: His hopes
Clytus, son of his old nurse
A march before daybreak for dinner, and a light dinner for supper

lessons.title: Chapter 96: The Gordian Knot
steps: Read Chapter XCVI, "The Gordian Knot," aloud together
Narration: tell about the Gordian knot and Alexander's trust in his doctor
Map work: Find Gordium in Phrygia, Tarsus, and the Cydnus River
Timeline: Add "Alexander cuts the Gordian knot" at 333 BC
questions: What was promised to whoever untied the Gordian knot?
What does "cutting the Gordian knot" mean today?
What did Alexander do with the warning letter about his doctor?
answers: Rule over all Asia
Solving a hard problem by a bold, direct action
Handed it to the doctor while he drank the medicine

lessons.title: Chapter 97: Alexander's Royal Captives
steps: Read Chapter XCVII, "Alexander's Royal Captives," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alexander treated the Persian royal family
Map work: Find Issus, at the corner of Asia Minor and Syria
Timeline: Add "Battle of Issus" at 333 BC
questions: Why did the queen mother kneel to the wrong man?
What did Alexander say about Hephaestion?
Why did Sisygambis cry when Alexander offered to teach spinning?
answers: Hephaestion was taller, and they wore plain armor
"He is my other self"
Persian royal ladies thought work was for slaves

lessons.title: Chapter 98: Alexander at Jerusalem
steps: Read Chapter XCVIII, "Alexander at Jerusalem," aloud together
Narration: tell about the siege of Tyre and Alexander's visit to Jerusalem
Map work: Find Damascus, Sidon, Tyre, and Jerusalem
Timeline: Add "Siege of Tyre" at 332 BC
questions: How did Alexander reach the island city of Tyre without a fleet?
Who came out to meet Alexander at Jerusalem?
answers: He built a causeway out to the island
The high priest Jaddua with the Levites
lessons.notes: The Jerusalem visit comes from the Jewish historian Josephus; many historians doubt it happened. The book tells it as fact, from a religious viewpoint. Tyre's punishment is grim.

lessons.title: Chapter 99: The African Desert
steps: Read Chapter XCIX, "The African Desert," aloud together
Narration: describe Alexander's march across the desert and the battle at Arbela
Map work: Find Alexandria in Egypt, the Siwa oasis in the Libyan desert, the Euphrates and Tigris rivers, and Arbela
Timeline: Add "Alexandria founded" at 331 BC and "Battle of Arbela (Gaugamela)" at 331 BC
questions: Which city did Alexander found at the mouth of the Nile?
What is a mirage?
How did the soldiers cross the Tigris?
answers: Alexandria
Seeing water and trees in the desert that are not really there
They swam, holding their shields over their heads

lessons.title: Chapter 100: Death of Darius
steps: Read Chapter C, "Death of Darius," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alexander changed after his victories and how Darius died
Map work: Find Babylon, Susa, and Persepolis
Timeline: Add "Persepolis burned; death of Darius III" at 330 BC
questions: What did Alexander find at Susa and send back to Athens?
Why did Alexander refuse to share Persia with Darius?
Who killed Darius?
answers: A bronze statue that Xerxes had carried off
He said the world could not have two masters any more than two suns
Bessus, one of his own followers

lessons.title: Chapter 101: Defeat of Porus
steps: Read Chapter CI, "Defeat of Porus," aloud together
Narration: tell how Alexander treated Porus
Map work: Find Persia, then northwest India and the Indus River region
Timeline: Add "Death of Clytus" at 328 BC and "Battle with Porus" at 326 BC
questions: Why did Alexander kill his friend Clytus?
What did Porus answer when asked how he wished to be treated?
What city did Alexander name after his horse?
answers: Clytus scolded him for his drinking, and Alexander struck him in a drunken rage
"Like a king!"
Bucephala

lessons.title: Chapter 102: The Return to Babylon
steps: Read Chapter CII, "The Return to Babylon," aloud together
Narration: tell why Alexander turned back and how his army and fleet returned
Map work: Find the Hyphasis and Indus rivers, the Indian Ocean coast, and the Persian Gulf
Timeline: Add "Army refuses to go on at the Hyphasis" at 326 BC and "Nearchus's voyage" at 325 BC
questions: Why did Alexander have to stop his conquests?
What did Alexander do with the little water his men brought him?
Why was Nearchus's voyage important?
answers: His soldiers refused to go any farther
Poured it on the sand, since his men could not drink too
It opened a sea route for trade with the East

lessons.title: Chapter 103: Death of Alexander the Great
steps: Read Chapter CIII, "Death of Alexander the Great," aloud together
Narration: tell about Alexander's last days and what he said about who should rule
Map work: Find Babylon, where Alexander died, and Alexandria, where he was buried
Timeline: Add "Death of Alexander the Great" at 323 BC
questions: How old was Alexander when he died?
Whom did Alexander say should have the throne?
Why did Ptolemy want Alexander's body in Egypt?
answers: Thirty-three
The strongest
An oracle said whoever buried Alexander would be master of his kingdom
lessons.notes: The mass weddings actually took place at Susa, and Hephaestion died at Ecbatana; the book moves both to Babylon.

lessons.title: Chapter 104: The Division of the Realm
steps: Read Chapter CIV, "The Division of the Realm," aloud together
Narration: tell how the generals tried to share Alexander's empire
Map work: Find Macedon, Babylon, and Egypt, and look at how huge the empire was
Timeline: Add "Generals divide Alexander's empire" at 323 BC
questions: Who were named to follow Alexander as king?
Into how many provinces was the kingdom divided?
answers: His half-brother Arridaeus and his baby son
Thirty-three

lessons.title: Chapter 105: Death of Demosthenes
steps: Read Chapter CV, "Death of Demosthenes," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Greeks revolted and how Demosthenes died
Map work: Find Lamia near Thermopylae and the island of Calauria (Poros), where Demosthenes died
Timeline: Add "Lamian War" at 323–322 BC and "Death of Demosthenes" at 322 BC
questions: What did Phocion say when people rushed to revolt?
How did Demosthenes escape being taken prisoner?
answers: If Alexander is dead today he will still be dead tomorrow, so there is time to think
He took poison hidden in his writing reed
lessons.notes: Describes a suicide; summarize if needed.

lessons.title: Chapter 106: The Last of the Athenians
steps: Read Chapter CVI, "The Last of the Athenians," aloud together
Narration: tell what happened to Perdiccas, Phocion, and Alexander's family
Map work: Find the Nile in Egypt, Athens, and Macedon
Timeline: Add "Death of Phocion" at 318 BC and "Alexander's son killed" at c. 310 BC
questions: How did Perdiccas die?
Why is Phocion called the "Last of the Athenians"?
answers: His soldiers turned on him after many were eaten by crocodiles crossing the Nile
He was the last great Athenian statesman; no one after him tried to win back the city's freedom

lessons.title: Chapter 107: The Colossus of Rhodes
steps: Read Chapter CVII, "The Colossus of Rhodes," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Colossus of Rhodes came to be built
Map work: Find the island of Rhodes, then mark the Seven Wonders on a map
Timeline: Add "Siege of Rhodes" at 305–304 BC and "Colossus of Rhodes" at c. 280–226 BC
questions: What nickname did Demetrius earn at Rhodes, and what does it mean?
What paid for the Colossus?
How was the Colossus destroyed?
answers: Poliorcetes, "the city taker"
Selling the war machines Demetrius left behind
An earthquake knocked it down
lessons.notes: The idea that ships sailed between its legs is a later legend. The book's list of wonders differs a little from the usual seven.

lessons.title: Chapter 108: The Battle of Ipsus
steps: Read Chapter CVIII, "The Battle of Ipsus," aloud together
Narration: tell how the Battle of Ipsus decided who got which part of the empire
Map work: Find Ipsus in Asia Minor, Egypt, Syria and Antioch, Thrace, and Macedon
Timeline: Add "Battle of Ipsus" at 301 BC
questions: Who ruled Egypt after Ipsus, and who was the last of his family?
How did the Athenians treat Demetrius after his defeat?
answers: Ptolemy; Cleopatra
They turned against him and made it a crime to speak well of him

lessons.title: Chapter 109: Demetrius and the Athenians
steps: Read Chapter CIX, "Demetrius and the Athenians," aloud together
Narration: tell how Demetrius surprised the Athenians, and how the Gauls were driven off
Map work: Find Athens, Delphi, and Galatia in Asia Minor
Timeline: Add "Demetrius takes Athens" at 295 BC and "Gauls attack Delphi" at 279 BC
questions: What did Demetrius do instead of punishing the Athenians?
Where did the defeated Gauls go?
answers: He forgave them and sent grain to every house
To a part of Asia Minor later called Galatia

units.title: Unit 15: The Last Days of Free Greece (Chapters 110–115)

lessons.title: Chapter 110: The Achæan League
steps: Read Chapter CX, "The Achæan League," aloud together
Narration: tell how Aratus freed Sicyon and captured the fortress of Corinth
Map work: Find Sicyon, Corinth, and Acrocorinth on the Isthmus
Timeline: Add "Aratus frees Sicyon" at 251 BC and "Acrocorinth captured" at 243 BC
questions: Where did young Aratus hide from the tyrant?
How many years in a row was Aratus chosen leader?
Why did Aratus pawn his wife's jewels?
answers: In the house of the tyrant's own sister
Thirty-five
To pay the man who showed the secret path up to Acrocorinth

lessons.title: Chapter 111: Division in Sparta
steps: Read Chapter CXI, "Division in Sparta," aloud together
Narration: tell what Agis tried to change in Sparta and how Chilonis stood by her family
Map work: Find Sparta in Laconia
Timeline: Add "Agis IV tries to reform Sparta" at c. 244 BC
questions: What did Agis want to do with the land and money?
How did Chilonis show loyalty?
answers: Divide it equally among the Spartans
She stayed with whichever of her father or husband was in trouble and followed him into exile

lessons.title: Chapter 112: Death of Agis
steps: Read Chapter CXII, "Death of Agis," aloud together
Narration: tell how Agis was betrayed and how Cleomenes carried on his plan
Map work: Find Sparta and Macedon
Timeline: Add "Death of Agis" at 241 BC and "Cleomenes' reforms" at 227 BC
questions: How was Agis caught?
Who taught Cleomenes about Agis's ideas?
What does the nickname "Doson" mean?
answers: Two false friends told the ephors he left the temple each night to bathe
Agiatis, Agis's widow, who became Cleomenes' wife
"Who will give," because he promised gifts he never gave

lessons.title: Chapter 113: The War of the Two Leagues
steps: Read Chapter CXIII, "The War of the Two Leagues," aloud together
Narration: tell how Aratus's mistake let Macedon and then Rome into Greece
Map work: Find Sellasia in Laconia, Aetolia, and Rome in Italy
Timeline: Add "Battle of Sellasia" at 222 BC and "Death of Aratus" at 213 BC
questions: Whom did Aratus ask for help against Sparta, and why was it a mistake?
To whom did the Spartans and Aetolians turn for help?
answers: The Macedonian king, who really wanted to rule Greece himself
Rome
lessons.notes: Includes the cruel "statue" of Nabis and a murder-suicide; preview. The order of events in this chapter is compressed.

lessons.title: Chapter 114: The Last of the Greeks
steps: Read Chapter CXIV, "The Last of the Greeks," aloud together
Narration: tell about Philopoemen, the "Last of the Greeks"
Map work: Find Megalopolis, Messenia, and Sparta
Timeline: Add "Death of Philopoemen" at 183 BC
questions: What happened when a hostess mistook Philopoemen for a servant?
Why is he called the "Last of the Greeks"?
What were his last words about?
answers: He calmly split wood as she asked
He was the last to try to keep Greece independent
He was glad the Achaean army had escaped safely

lessons.title: Chapter 115: Greece a Roman Province
steps: Read Chapter CXV, "Greece a Roman Province," aloud together
Narration: tell how Greece went from being "freed" by Rome to being ruled by it
Map work: Find Corinth and the Isthmus, Macedon, and Rome
Timeline: Add "Flamininus proclaims Greek freedom" at 196 BC and "Corinth destroyed; Greece under Rome" at 146 BC. Look back over your whole timeline
questions: What did the Roman consul announce at the Isthmian games?
What happened to Corinth?
What name did the Romans give the province of Greece?
answers: That Rome had beaten the king of Macedon and the Greek states were free
It was burned and its art carried off to Rome
Achaia
lessons.notes: Corinth was destroyed by the Roman general Mummius, not Aemilius Paulus, who had defeated Macedon in 168 BC.
